Applying by the December or January admissions deadline, whichever is relevant to the course
No restrictions on nationality or country of ordinary residence

existing.eligibility_summary: Open to candidates applying for a new full-time or part-time DPhil or Master's course at Oxford by the December or January deadline for their course, in any subject area, with no restriction on nationality or country of ordinary residence. Applicants must not already hold a deferred graduate offer and must not be continuing the same degree at Oxford in the next year.
benefits: Full course fee coverage for Home and Overseas fee status students
Annual living expenses grant of at least the UKRI minimum doctoral stipend rate
Study support grant for part-time study
No separate application, nomination or extra documentation
Access to the Clarendon scholar community of about 700 on-course scholars from around 70 nations
coverage: Course fees covered in full for Home and Overseas fee status students
Annual grant for living expenses of at least the UKRI minimum doctoral stipend rate (at least Â£20,780 in 2025-26) for full-time scholars
Study support grant for part-time scholars, worth a sixth, a third or half of the UKRI minimum doctoral stipend rate depending on course nature and duration
Certain modular fee structure components for part-time courses: Annual Award Fee (maximum two years), Registration Fee and Dissertation Fee
requirements: Apply to your Oxford course by the December or January deadline relevant to that course
Submit no separate scholarship application - consideration is automatic
Do not hold a deferred graduate offer at the time of application
Meet the academic bar of the course as well as the Clarendon selection criteria
Accept the Clarendon offer letter (CB1) once issued
documents: Oxford graduate application for the chosen course (the only application needed)
Transcripts and references as required by the chosen course
No additional documents are required for Clarendon itself
application_method: Single Oxford graduate application through the University's application portal
existing.selection_notes: Selection criteria vary slightly by subject area and by taught versus research degree. The University states its only goal is 'to choose the best students worldwide, as decided by experts in each student's field'. Academics in the department assess academic quality, nominate to the division, and the divisions assess nominations 'on their academic merit and future potential', shortlisting the top-ranked departmental nominees.
existing.best_fit: Applicants with an outstanding academic record (typically a first class honours degree or equivalent) seeking fully funded postgraduate study at Oxford in any subject, with no restriction on nationality.
existing.notes: The Â£20,780 figure is the published floor for the 2025-26 living expenses grant for full-time scholars and is separate from the full course fee coverage. Continuation charges levied after the period of fee liability are not covered by the Clarendon Fund. Part-time scholars receive a study support grant instead of the full living grant, worth a sixth, a third or half of the UKRI minimum doctoral stipend rate.
existing.duration: Normally the scholar's period of fee liability; at the discretion of the academic divisions some awards extend beyond it with only the living grant paid in the extra period
existing.application_period: Annual, tied to the Oxford graduate course deadlines. Applicants to degree-bearing courses applying by the December or January deadline for their course are automatically considered. Departmental nominations are reviewed by the academic divisions in February or March.
existing.deadline_display: There is no separate Clarendon deadline: you must apply to your Oxford course by the December or January admissions deadline, whichever is relevant to your course. 'You do not need to submit any additional documents and there are no separate scholarship application forms for Clarendon.'
existing.program_type: Doctoral and taught postgraduate scholarship scheme based on academic merit

eligibility: Applying to start a new full-time graduate course at Oxford
Ordinarily resident in one of the eligible countries, mainly developing and emerging economies
Intending to return to your country of ordinary residence once the course is completed

Able to demonstrate a connection between the subject of study and longer-term career objectives, explaining how the professional work will contribute to the improvement of public life in the country of origin or at a wider regional or international level
Outstanding university graduate or professional who would not otherwise be able to support themselves to study at Oxford
Must be offered a place on an eligible course
Applicants who indicated refugee or displaced status at application are considered eligible if their nationality meets the country eligibility criteria
existing.eligibility_summary: Applicants must be starting a new full-time graduate course at Oxford, ordinarily resident in an eligible country (mainly developing and emerging economies), intending to return to their country of ordinary residence after the course, and able to connect their subject of study to longer-term career objectives improving public life. Deferred 2027-28 offers and current Oxford students (unless already Weidenfeld-Hoffmann scholars) are excluded.
benefits: Living costs grant of at least Â£21,805
One-year leadership development programme with philosophical discussions, business skills and communication training
Possible transfer to a partner college that contributes to the scholarship funding
coverage: Grant for living costs of at least Â£21,805
Leadership development programme over the course of a year, including philosophical discussions, business skills and communication training
Long-term mentoring and networking through the Weidenfeld-Hoffmann Trust
requirements: Select the Weidenfeld-Hoffmann Scholarships and Leadership Programme in the Scholarships section of the Oxford graduate application form
Submit the graduate application by the December or January deadline for your course
Complete and upload the Weidenfeld-Hoffmann Scholarships Statement 2027/28 by the same deadline
Provide accurate nationality and ordinary residence details, which are used to assess country eligibility
Be available for an interview, likely held online in April 2027
Accept an offer of a place on an eligible course
documents: Oxford graduate application form with the Weidenfeld-Hoffmann Scholarships and Leadership Programme selected in the Scholarships section
Weidenfeld-Hoffmann Scholarships Statement 2027/28 (official PDF, uploaded with the application)
Any documents required by the chosen course
application_method: Oxford graduate application form with the scholarship selected
Upload of the Weidenfeld-Hoffmann Scholarships Statement 2027/28
existing.selection_notes: All eligibility criteria are assessed during the selection process using the graduate application form, the Weidenfeld-Hoffmann Scholarships Statement and, where relevant, the interview. The programme selects candidates judged to have the potential to become leaders who will improve public life in their country or region. Partner colleges may transfer successful candidates to a partner college to take up the scholarship.
existing.best_fit: Outstanding graduates and professionals from eligible developing and emerging economies who intend to return home and can articulate how their field of study will improve public life in their country or region.
existing.notes: Funding is split between the University (40%) and donors to the Weidenfeld-Hoffmann Trust (60%). The programme was established in 2015 and doubled in size in 2017 after a Â£9m donation from AndrÃ© Hoffmann matched by Â£6m from Oxford. Partner schemes with the Oxford Pakistan Programme and Chevening are managed separately by the Trust, but applying for this programme constitutes consent to be considered for them. The full eligible-courses and eligible-countries lists are collapsed sections on the page and were not expanded, so the exact country and course lists were not transcribed.
existing.duration: The full duration of the fee liability for the agreed course
existing.application_period: 2027/28 cycle. Applications must be submitted by the December or January deadline for the chosen course; shortlisted applicants are interviewed online, likely in April 2027; decisions are expected by the end of May 2027.
existing.deadline_display: Submit your application for graduate study by the relevant December or January deadline for your course, together with the Weidenfeld-Hoffmann Scholarships Statement. Applications held over after the December or January deadline, or placed on a waiting list, are not eligible for scholarship consideration.
existing.program_type: Fully-funded graduate scholarship with a leadership development programme
